analyst_view.overall: Rio Ave are 16th with two league wins and the most goals conceded (23), having conceded at least twice in each of their five home games; Vasco Seabra took over in October. Braga (8th, 14 points) beat Famalicão 3-0 under new coach Franclim Carvalho but have not scored in their last five away games, and drew 0-0 at Aarhus on Thursday despite 26 shots. Rio Ave's André Ntoi is suspended; Braga have Barcia and Gabriel Silva back, with only Niakaté out.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals, with Braga expected to score twice. Rio Ave's home defence is the worst in the league, but Braga haven't scored away in five games. These pull in opposite directions, so we stay with the site.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners. Braga had 26 shots against Aarhus without scoring, and Carvalho wants pace, intensity and attacking play; a side dominating without finishing tends to win plenty of corners. We lean slightly higher.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards. Rio Ave are fighting relegation and have had a red card recently (Ntoi), but we found nothing specific on referee Cláudio Pereira, so we keep the site's figure.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.1 shots, already raised by Braga's recent volume. Braga had 26 shots in Denmark on Thursday and face the league's leakiest defence, and Carvalho says Braga must be the favourites and attack. We lean slightly higher.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 shots on target. Braga create a lot but their finishing away from home has been poor, so we stay with the site.
